transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're at 15:00 Pacific, running 42 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena Patel: Lena here, Jun and Omar on our side.
[00:12] Jun Park: Jun, ML eng.
[00:14] Dr. Omar Khan: Omar, clinical ops.
[00:18] Diego Ramirez: Diego from Redwood, SE.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Priya, CSM.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: quality eval results, regressions after v2 quantized model, guardrail tuning, and next steps. We posted the scoring sheet link in the calendar notes.
[00:35] Lena Patel: Saw that, thanks. We saw a small uptick in hallucination FP on the discharge summary prompts after you switched to the 4-bit profile.
[00:45] Diego Ramirez: Yeah, we expected some shift; quantization and kernel path changes can change tokenization edge cases, also the continuous batching latency optimizations sometimes alter prefix attention margins. We ran the automatic calibration but looks like two clusters popped up.
[00:59] Jun Park: Can you describe the clusters? We flagged them in our own eval.
[01:05] Diego Ramirez: Sure, cluster A is named-entity truncation where the model drops secondary medication mentions — usually lower-frequency tokens. Cluster B is a factual mismatch where dates or dosages are swapped, likely due to subtle beam search scoring differences post-quant.
[01:20] Dr. Omar Khan: That second one is risky for clinical notes. Even 1-2% is a concern.
[01:25] Maya Chen: Agreed. That's why today's regression check is focused on those. Quick reminder of the scoring rubric: we have exact match for structured fields, clinical accuracy score (0-3), and harm flagging. The CSV Diego shared has the per-prompt per-example scores.
[01:41] Jun Park: We ran the new prompt set v3 and compared to v2. v3 improved recall on problems list but precision dropped a bit, which is expected.
[01:50] Lena Patel: Also saw more conservative output when we added the explicit do-not-invent guardrail in the system prompt.
[01:57] Diego Ramirez: Right, guardrails do help but they can also cause under-generation. We discussed a dynamic guardrail where you only apply the do-not-invent after the model confidence falls below threshold — confidence being the token-level logit gap metric we added to the scoring.
[02:13] Jun Park: How stable is that logit-gap metric across sequence length? Our discharge summaries vary a lot.
[02:19] Diego Ramirez: There's some decay but we normalize per-token and per-prefix length. On the Redwood runtime, the KV cache handling during long sequence runs can slightly change logits, so normalization helps. Note: the runtime path for dedicated vs hosted can differ; in Dedicated we observed slightly lower variance.
[02:36] Lena Patel: Are you recommending Dedicated for stability? Our initial ask was hosted for speed to market.
[02:42] Maya Chen: Hosted is fine for early pilot; Dedicated is worth evaluating if you need strict latency/variance SLOs. We can run a small dedicated trial if desired.
[02:51] Dr. Omar Khan: Budget might be tight. We want to first see if prompt + guardrails fix the regressions.
[02:58] Priya Singh: We'll prioritize prompt tuning, then decide on infra.
[03:02] Maya Chen: Good. Back to regressions — Diego, did you prototype a patch?
[03:07] Diego Ramirez: Yes, two things. One: adjust the beam scoring temperature and apply an entity-preservation loss during rerank; two: a post-processing rule that re-checks medication token spans against the original text and falls back to a conservative extractive path if mismatch confidence is low. We tested on 500 examples: medication span recovery improved by ~12 percentage points.
[03:29] Jun Park: That's promising. But what's the false positive shift?
[03:33] Diego Ramirez: FP rose slightly for non-medication fields but still within tolerable range; for medications we decreased FP. Full numbers are in the scoring sheet.
[03:40] Lena Patel: One data point: example row 237 in the spreadsheet shows the model inventing a follow-up appointment date — flagged as high harm.
[03:48] Diego Ramirez: I remember that case; fallback rule fixed it in the rerank. That case is included in action item tests.
[03:54] Maya Chen: OK let's walk through the scoring thresholds we propose: clinical accuracy threshold 0.85, harm flag rate <0.5%, and an EM for structured fields >0.9. Those are pilot targets, not production SLAs.
[04:10] Jun Park: 0.85 clinical accuracy seems aggressive for discharge summaries given current dataset. Can we relax to 0.8 until second round of prompt tuning?
[04:18] Dr. Omar Khan: I support 0.8, and then plan to get to 0.85 after tuning.
[04:23] Maya Chen: Fine, set initial target 0.8, with step-up to 0.85 after Diego's tuning. We'll reflect that in next steps.
[04:31] Priya Singh: Quick note on privacy — we still need the signed DPA and SOC2 docs. Lena, did you get the SOC2 link?
[04:38] Lena Patel: I saw the link. We'll push SOC2 review to legal next week.
[04:42] Maya Chen: I'll resend the SOC2 and network diagram.
[04:45] Diego Ramirez: Back to regression detection: we propose an automated daily regression check that runs new commits and quantization variants on a canonical prompt set (the one in the spreadsheet). It emails summaries and highlights new failure clusters with example IDs.
[04:58] Jun Park: That would be super useful. We can triage quickly.
[05:02] Lena Patel: Can you include tolerances so we don't get noise?
[05:06] Diego Ramirez: Yes, we'll add minimum effect size and require contiguous cluster size > 5 examples to trigger an alert.
[05:14] Jun Park: For guardrails, can we tune on de-identified EHR and also synthetic edge cases?
[05:21] Diego Ramirez: Absolutely, synthetic adversarial examples are part of the eval harness. Please upload 2k de-id rows and we'll include them.
[05:28] Jun Park: Will do.
[05:29] Dr. Omar Khan: On the scoring spreadsheet, can we add a clinical reviewer column so we can track human disagreements?
[05:36] Priya Singh: Good idea. We'll add a reviewer column and a free-text notes field.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Anything else on quality?
[05:42] Lena Patel: A small UX ask — the model sometimes outputs markdown tables that our downstream parser chokes on. We could ask for consistent JSON outputs for structured extracts.
[05:50] Diego Ramirez: We can push a structured output schema and enforce via the Redwood function-calling style or structured output support; that reduces parser errors.
[05:58] Jun Park: Are function-calls available on hosted?
[06:00] Diego Ramirez: Yes, hosted supports structured output and function-calling; on private deployments we can mirror the same interface. Sometimes the transcription in our notes calls it 'function calls' as 'funct'n- call', sorry bad auto-transcription on earlier notes.
[06:14] Maya Chen: Okay, plan: Diego to run the regression harness on v2 and v2-quant with the new rerank + fallback, include synthetic adversarial set, and share results. Maya will send updated prompt set (v3b) and guardrail wording. Jun will upload de-id EHR.
[06:29] Jun Park: Quick question about latency — guardrails and rerank add extra compute, what's the hit?
[06:34] Diego Ramirez: In our test on c5-like instances with batching disabled, rerank added ~80ms median; if we use lightweight rerank (scoring only top-3) it drops to ~30ms. Caching reduces repeated prefix costs.
[06:47] Lena Patel: For our SLA we need p95 < 700ms for summaries; will adding rerank break that?
[06:54] Diego Ramirez: Probably not for typical 512-token summaries if we tune the rerank. We'll include latency in the benchmark.
[07:01] Dr. Omar Khan: Any security blockers for data share?
[07:05] Maya Chen: We support S3 encrypted uploads and can accept a mounted SFTP. We'll provide KMS integration details.
[07:11] Jun Park: We'll redact PHI as discussed and provide the de-id set.
[07:16] Priya Singh: I'll coordinate the DPA signature and SOC2 access.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Great. Before we wrap, let's capture the regression examples and assign owners.
[07:25] Diego Ramirez: Action item: Diego to produce a CSV of top 50 regression examples, labeled by cluster, with suggested fix type.
[07:32] Maya Chen: Maya to update the prompt set (v3b) and push to the scoring sheet.
[07:36] Jun Park: Jun to upload de-id EHR subset.
[07:40] Lena Patel: Lena to share legal timeline for SOC2 and DPA review.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Anything else?
[07:47] Dr. Omar Khan: Nope, thanks everyone.
[07:50] Maya Chen: OK we'll follow up with the updated spreadsheet and Diego's regression report by next Thursday.
[07:57] Priya Singh: I'll send calendar invites for the benchmark run and for a 30-minute follow-up once results are in.
[08:04] Maya Chen: Thanks all. End call.
